title: Protective Roles of Zinc and Selenium Against Oxidative Stress in Brain Endothelial Cells Under Shear Stress.
authors: Branca, Jacopo J V; Gulisano, Massimo; Pacini, Alessandra
one_liner_zh: 该文研究锌和硒对脑内皮细胞在剪切应力下氧化应激的保护作用，仅涉及NRF2转录因子核转位作为氧化应激标志物，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a major risk factor for cerebrovascular diseases due to its damaging effects on the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and associated pathologies. Oxidative stress-induced endothelial damage plays a critical role in BBB disruption, potentially leading to cognitive impairment and neurodegeneration. In this study, we investigated the protective effects of two essential trace elements, zinc (Zn) and selenium (Se), against oxidative stress in human brain endothelial cells (HBCE5i) exposed to hypertensive shear stress. Using an innovative millifluidic system (LiveBox2), which allows for the precise simulation of continuous flow conditions, we replicated the hemodynamic forces associated with hypertension. METHODS: Cells were treated with ZnCl(2) (5-50 microM) or Na(2)SeO(3) (50-500 nM) at concentrations selected based on previous studies and confirmed by cytotoxicity assays. RESULTS: Our results demonstrated that shear stress significantly altered the localization of the tight junction protein zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1) and induced the nuclear translocation of the transcription factor NRF2, a hallmark of oxidative stress. Importantly, treatment with 10 microM ZnCl(2) preserved ZO-1 membrane localization and prevented NRF2 translocation, as confirmed by quantitative image analysis. In contrast, Na(2)SeO(3) did not provide comparable protection, although modest improvements in ZO-1 localization were observed in some replicates. DISCUSSION: We discuss potential reasons for selenium's limited efficacy, including differences in bioavailability and cellular uptake. Our findings underscore zinc's promising role as a neurovascular protector and suggest that further investigation into more complex in vitro models and in vivo studies is warranted.
abstract_zh: 背景：高血压是脑血管疾病的主要危险因素，因其对血脑屏障（BBB）及其相关病理的损害作用。氧化应激诱导的内皮损伤在BBB破坏中起关键作用，可能导致认知障碍和神经退行性变。在本研究中，我们探讨了两种必需微量元素锌（Zn）和硒（Se）对暴露于高血压剪切应力的人脑内皮细胞（HBCE5i）中氧化应激的保护作用。利用创新的毫流控系统（LiveBox2），该系统能够精确模拟连续流动条件，我们复制了与高血压相关的血流动力学力。方法：细胞用ZnCl(2)（5-50微摩尔）或Na(2)SeO(3)（50-500纳摩尔）处理，浓度基于先前研究选择并通过细胞毒性试验确认。结果：我们的结果表明，剪切应力显著改变了紧密连接蛋白zonula occludens-1（ZO-1）的定位，并诱导转录因子NRF2的核转位，这是氧化应激的标志。重要的是，10微摩尔ZnCl(2)处理保留了ZO-1的膜定位并阻止了NRF2转位，这通过定量图像分析得到确认。相比之下，Na(2)SeO(3)未提供相当的保护，尽管在某些重复中观察到ZO-1定位的适度改善。讨论：我们讨论了硒疗效有限的可能原因，包括生物利用度和细胞摄取的差异。我们的发现强调了锌作为神经血管保护剂的潜在作用，并建议进一步研究更复杂的体外模型和体内研究是必要的。
